title: Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake appoints new superintendent - NewsBreak
text:
By Natalie St. Denis ,
1 hours ago
BURNT HILLS, N.Y. ( NEWS10 ) — The Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake Board of Education has appointed the district’s new superintendent. Dr. Christopher Abdoo was named as the next leader at a special meeting on Wednesday.
Download our WTEN+ streaming app on Roku, Fire TV and Apple TV! Abdoo’s appointment comes after an extensive search following Dr. Patrick McGrath Jr.’s retirement announcement in October 2025 . After serving as the district’s superintendent for 14 years, McGrath is slated to retire at the end of the school year.
Dr. Christopher Abdoo (Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake School District) School officials feel confident in Abdoo’s ability to step up to the plate. He currently serves as Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake’s Assistant Superintendent for Support Services. He also has more than 25 years of experience in public education and a background in operational leadership, school finance and institutional organization.
“Dr. Abdoo’s professional experience, along with 14 years of district knowledge, showed the entire board his deep commitment to students and staff, his collaborative leadership style, and his clear understanding of how to lead a district through both opportunity and growth. His experience and values align closely with our community’s expectations for excellence,” said School Board President Don Marshall.
In his current role as assistant superintendent for support services, he helps the superintendent of schools with direction, coordination, planning, operation and evaluation of BH-BL’s educational programming. His also oversees more than 300 non-instructional BH-BL personnel, the operation and maintenance of district facilities, the school lunch program, the student transportation program, accounting and payroll operations, purchasing operations, district security, technology operations and community use of facilities.
Abdoo serves as the lead evaluator of teacher evaluations across the five district buildings. He also participates in all district contract negotiations with collective bargaining organizations, carries out long and short range financial planning for the district as a whole, guides the district in school environment safety, insurance and risk management decisions and has oversight of all financial reporting. In collaboration with the superintendent and shared-decision making committees, he also led the large-scale school improvement and renovation projects within the district in 2013, 2018 and 2023.

Outside of the district, he serves as an executive coach for doctoral candidates at Russell Sage College, where he has also been an adjunct professor in the Educational Leadership program since 2019. Abdoo was also the 2025 New York State recipient of the Association of School Business Officials (ASBO) Volunteer Service Award and serves on the Board of Directors for ASBO-New York. He is a published author of journal articles on teacher recruitment and retention as well as effective collaboration among board members and central administration.
Before joining the BH-BL administrative team, Abdoo served as the director of business and finance for the Rome City School District and the business administrator for the Frankfort-Schuyler Central School District. He was also a social studies teacher at the New Hartford Central School District and an accountant and auditor for the Ernst & Young LLP’s Manhattan office.
He holds a B.S. in accounting from Binghamton University, an M.S. in social studies education from Syracuse University, a Certificate of Advanced Study in Educational Administration/Leadership from the State University of New York College at Cortland and a Doctorate of Education from the Sage Colleges. His doctoral dissertation focused on factors that influenced the recruitment and retention of teachers in the Capital Region.
Abdoo lives in the district with his wife and their two daughters.
“I am profoundly honored and deeply grateful for the trust the Board of Education has placed in me,” said Abdoo. “Having been a dedicated member of this community for 14 years, I am excited to continue partnering with our exceptional students, administrators, faculty, staff, and families. My commitment is to continue to uphold and advance the tradition of excellence that defines the Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake School District, guiding us forward through both opportunity and change so that we continue to provide a world-class educational experience for all of our students.”
He will begin his new role as superintendent of schools on July 1.
